content_preview.title: Novee Security Finds Zero-Privilege Flaws in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex Around Black Hat USA 2026
content_preview.summary: Researcher Elad Meged showed a privilege-less GitHub issue could reach CI secrets in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex; two flaws got CVEs, one didn't.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A GitHub issue opened by an account with no repository privileges was enough to reach CI runner secrets in AI coding agents built by three of the industry's largest vendors, according to research from [Novee Security](https://novee.security/blog/critical-flaws-in-anthropic-google-and-openais-coding-agents/) published around Black Hat USA 2026. Researcher Elad Meged, described on the company's blog as Novee's founding engineer and security researcher, found separate exploitable flaws...

editor_notes.content_quality: Thorough, well-organized News piece covering three separate vendor vulnerabilities with a shared root cause. Correctly separates each vendor's flaw (CVE, CVSS scores from both NVD and vendor scoring, fix version) and attributes overlapping claims to their specific sources rather than blending them.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 successful snapshots directly, plus WebFetch verification for the 2 bot-blocked sources. Novee's own blog (source-0) confirms the founding-engineer byline, the full multi-paragraph Codex-fix quote verbatim, and the 'well over a hundred' repositories figure verbatim. The Hacker News (source-1) confirms the zero-privilege GitHub-issue framing. Both NVD records (source-4, source-5) confirm CVE numbers, affected version ranges, CVSS v3.1/v4 scores from both NIST and the vendor CNA, and the technical vulnerability descriptions verbatim. The Cloud Security Alliance research note (source-6) confirms the Black Hat USA 2026 / August 5 presentation date and the 'harness is the code between the model and the real world' quote verbatim -- its suspicious_patterns flag was investigated and confirmed a false positive (see findings). SC World (source-7) confirms all three attributed quotes verbatim. GBHackers and Cyberpress (both bot-blocked, no archive.org fallback) were independently verified via WebFetch -- every claim attributed to each matches verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (CVE numbers, CVSS scores, affected version ranges, fix versions, quotes) verify against their cited sources. No hallucinations or misattributions found.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate of existing archive content. Note: this is one of two independently-written submissions on this exact story (also PR #2206). This one has broader sourcing (8 sources vs. 5) and is being approved as the canonical article; PR #2206 should be reviewed against this one for rejection as a duplicate once this merges.
recommendations: Added novee.security and labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org to config/source_allowlist.txt as legitimate primary/research sources. Left cyberpress.org off the allowlist pending stronger confidence in its editorial standing; its one claim was independently verified via WebFetch instead.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve. Every claim verified across all 8 sources (6 direct, 2 via WebFetch fallback); the automated suspicious_patterns flag was investigated and confirmed a false positive rather than a genuine injection attempt. No corrections needed.
